tools.name: signup
tools.description: Explicit signup, for a client that cannot keep a session across calls: create a tenant and receive a bearer key and namespace. Unauthenticated. Most clients never need this -- any other host.*/billing.* call from a fresh connection creates a tenant implicitly and returns its own /u/<secret>/mcp URL

Read-only -- this call alone never creates a tenant. Call this

tools.name: host.help.search
tools.description: Search this host's own documentation and tool descriptions. Returns up to k hits (default 3, response under 2 KB), each with a snippet, the nearest runnable example and an anchor. Read-only, anonymous, no tenant data -- call it with the error text or import line you are stuck on before reading any d

tools.name: host.help.get
tools.description: Return the documentation section an anchor points at: its text (at most 4 KB) and its first fenced example. Pass an anchor exactly as an error, hint or help entry printed it, e.g. a rate_limited error's `anchor`. Read-only, anonymous, no tenant data. An unknown anchor is anchor_not_found with the ne

tools.name: host.errors
tools.description: List every error code this host can return, each with its class (agent_fault | host_refusal | upstream_fault | plan_limit | host_fault), family, remedy, docs anchor, retryable flag and help_url -- the same object GET /errors.json serves. Pass code to get one row; a misspelt code answers tool_not_fou

tools.name: host.redeem
tools.description: Exchange a signup(handoff: true) handoff_token for the tenant key it was issued for. Single-use: a second redemption fails with handoff_token_redeemed; past its expiry it fails with handoff_token_expired. Unauthenticated -- the token itself is the proof.

tools.name: billing.plans
tools.description: The plan catalog (price and quotas per plan) and whether Stripe billing is configured on this host. Anonymous callers get the same answer as tenants.

tools.name: host.whoami
tools.description: Return the calling tenant's identity, including key_age_s and key_rotated_at for auditing credential hygiene.

tools.name: host.tool_publish
tools.description: Publish a tool of a registered kind (e.g. python, http or echo; the kind argument's enum lists them all) under this tenant's namespace. Call host.quickstart(kind) first for a filled-in example spec and the full publish-to-call sequence. Python's sandbox API: import mcphost (mcphost.table, mcphost.st

tools.name: host.tool_call
tools.description: Invoke a tool this tenant has already published, by its local name -- the same real, metered call as calling it directly by its namespaced name (<namespace>.<name>), for a session that has no way to see its own namespaced tool name yet. Unlike host.tool_test, this counts toward host.usage and appear

tools.name: host.tool_test
tools.description: Dry-run a published tool by name: verdict (pass/will_fail/unverifiable), writes rolled back (dry_run); see host.quickstart.

tools.name: host.state.set
tools.description: Write one key in this tenant's key-value state namespace; value may be any JSON value. Overrun of the plan's state_bytes_max quota fails with state_quota_exceeded and writes nothing.

tools.name: host.state.get
tools.description: Read one key from this tenant's key-value state namespace. Returns found: false (not an error) if the key was never set.

tools.name: host.state.list
tools.description: List keys (with their current values) in this tenant's key-value state namespace, optionally filtered by prefix.

tools.name: host.tool_share
tools.description: Share one of this tenant's published tools with everyone (visibility: "public") or with a named group this tenant owns (visibility: "group", group: <name>). The tool keeps running in this tenant's own sandbox with this tenant's own secrets; a caller reaches it as <this tenant's namespace>.<name>.

tools.name: host.feedback.send
tools.description: Tell the host's humans what you needed: kind, up to 2048 bytes of text, optional context. Works before signup. Returns feedback_id.

tools.name: host.feedback.list
tools.description: List your own feedback (newest first, status received). Anonymous callers get [].

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: signup · Private data: signup, host.help.search, host.redeem, host.whoami, host.tool_share · Public sink: host.tool_publish, host.tool_share, host.feedback.send · Destructive: host.quickstart, host.tool_test.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: signup · Private data: signup, host.help.search, host.redeem, host.whoami, host.tool_share · Public sink: host.tool_publish, host.tool_share, host.feedback.send · Destructive: host.quickstart, host.tool_test

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
